analyst.summary: CMS Info Systems, India's #1 cash-logistics player (~46% ATM cash-management share), had a real, not cosmetic, bad FY26: revenue growth collapsed to 2.6% (from a 9.1% 3-year CAGR), EBITDA fell 5.2%, PAT fell 18.5% to Rs 303 crore, and working-capital quality deteriorated, driven mainly by repeated delays to a large SBI cash-outsourcing contract (~Rs 150cr revenue hit), an AGS-exit-related disruption in the offsite-ATM market, and one-off wage costs. The key fact for an existing holding: the SBI contract (Rs 1,000cr/10-year, 5,000 ATMs) went live in January 2026, Q4 FY26 already shows a sharp sequential recovery (services revenue record-high, margin +280bp QoQ, PAT +38% QoQ), and management guides FY27 total revenue growth of 13-17% (services 17-21%). The PE-sponsor (Baring/Sion) fully exited by mid-2025 with no residual overhang, CEO Rajiv Kaul has been raising his personal stake, and the company just completed a 9x-oversubscribed Rs 168 crore buyback plus a Rs 5.25/share dividend off a net-cash balance sheet. India's currency-in-circulation continues to grow in absolute terms despite UPI's scale, so the cash-logistics TAM is not obviously collapsing on a 3-year view, though bank ATM-network rationalization and tougher re-tender pricing are real structural risks. At ~14.5-14.7x trailing earnings against a depressed FY26 base, the -47.8% drawdown looks more like the market extrapolating one bad, largely-resolved year into a permanent growth reset than a re-rating on new structural information. Judgment call: Hold, with genuine two-way risk that the Principal should be aware of.
